- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves in history; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment >0.67, apply 70% weight to recent price; if <0.33, apply 80% weight to prior 7-day average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
